mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in every one of the last four weekly means (-29.3, -28.7, -27.1, -27.0), showing persistent reopening momentum that has not yet exhausted itself; this persistence carries the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 2.3 points across the four weekly means with no down week
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to -28.0 percent change from baseline, the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES fell 2.1 points at t-0w (-19.9 to -22.0), the first contraction after three weeks of gains; a shrinking commuter base removes weekday lunch, errand and after-work footfall, dragging the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by >= 2.0 percent-change points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -19.9 at t-1w to -22.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with partial office return
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES declines by >= 2.0 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC still rises over the following 28 days in more than half of observations.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS recovered 3.6 points over the window while TRANSIT stayed flat at -12.6; when discretionary outdoor trips expand but transit use is capped, the marginal trip is a short local trip that lands in stores, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -25.9 to -22.3 while TRANSIT held at -12.6 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls over the next 28 days while the PARKS minus TRANSIT gap widens by 2 or more points.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week window sits inside the seasonal shift toward warmer weather, which lifts outdoor and storefront activity; PARKS and RETAIL_REC both trend upward in the snapshot, and this seasonal lift raises the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean above the last.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 3.6 points and RETAIL_REC improved 2.3 points over the four weekly means
failure_condition: PARKS and RETAIL_REC both decline across the next four weekly means relative to the last four.

mechanism_narrative: Under a capacity-capped reopening regime, GROCERY_PHARM has plateaued (3.6 to 3.4) while WORKPLACES remains below -20; the remaining retail gap is supply- and capacity-constrained rather than demand-constrained, so RETAIL_REC cannot advance and the next 28-day mean is lower than the last.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM four-week absolute change is < 0.5 points while WORKPLACES stays below -20
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM plateaued at 3.6 then 3.4 while WORKPLACES sat at -22.0
regime_hint: capacity-capped reopening with occupancy limits still binding
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds the last 28-day mean in more than half of windows where GROCERY_PHARM is flat and WORKPLACES is below -20.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossed above -13 for the first time in the window (-14.1 to -12.6) and held there for two consecutive weeks; sustained transit crossings mark the point where discretionary trips resume, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean exceeds -13.0 in two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -14.1 at t-2w to -12.6 at t-1w and stayed at -12.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the week after TRANSIT holds above -13.0 for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC is lower than in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC improved 2.3 points while WORKPLACES worsened 2.1 points over the same four weeks, so retail activity is being carried by non-commute trips; while this divergence persists, the leisure-driven component keeps the next 28-day mean above the last.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 2.3 points while WORKPLACES fell 2.1 points between t-3w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days in windows where RETAIL_REC improved while WORKPLACES fell over the prior four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has held at or above 5.0 in all four weeks while GROCERY_PHARM plateaued near 3.5, the signature of households staying local; under a stay-at-home-adjacent regime, retail-and-recreation trips stay suppressed and the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the last.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays >= 5.0 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was flat at 5.6 for the last two weeks while GROCERY_PHARM slipped from 3.6 to 3.4
regime_hint: stay-at-home adjacent, restrictions only partially lifted
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds the last 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 5.0 for four consecutive weeks.
